note: UN pack item (subtopic un_system): headquarters New York, Charter signed 26 June 1945, in force 24 October 1945 (UN Day), 193 member states, six principal organs, ICJ at The Hague as the only principal organ outside New York. All elements taught in sections 'founding' and 'principal_organs' from NCERT leps106, IGNOU Unit 12 and MEA sources (claims c01, c02, c06, c13, c43-c45).

Geneva cluster pack item. PARTIALLY taught: ILO created 1919 and its tripartite structure (c31, c32) and ITU founded 1865 (c33) are taught; but the Geneva headquarters city for ILO/WHO/WMO/ITU, WHO 1948, UNHCR 1950 and WMO 1950 were not present in any fetched NCERT/IGNOU/MEA/PIB source (PIB confirms only that ILO's Governing Body meets in Geneva), so they are not asserted in this chapter.

Paris/Rome/New York pack item. PARTIALLY taught: UNESCO headquarters Paris is taught (PIB, c50, c55) and UNICEF/UNDP/WFP are covered as programmes with India's contributor status (c42). Not taught: UNESCO's 1945/46 founding dates, FAO Rome 1945, WFP Rome 1961, UNICEF New York 1946 and UNDP 1965 — none appeared in the fetched allowed sources, so they are disclosed as a gap rather than asserted.

Vienna/Nairobi/Montreal/London pack item. Not taught: IAEA Vienna 1957, UNIDO Vienna 1966, UNEP Nairobi 1972, ICAO Montreal and IMO London headquarters/founding facts were not present in any fetched NCERT/IGNOU/MEA/PIB page. UNEP is taught only by function (environment monitoring, c34). NCERT supports only that the IAEA is the agency for safety and peaceful use of nuclear technology (exercise), with no headquarters or year.

Real WBCS 2017 prelims item: which state does not have veto power (answer: Canada). Taught via the P-5 list and the rule that only permanent members hold the veto (c08, c10); also drilled in practice question q17.
Real Clerkship 2023 (Session IV) item: which country does NOT have veto power (answer: Canada). Same teaching as the WBCS 2017 item (c08, c10, q17).

Real Clerkship 2023 (Session IV) item asking which country was NOT elected a non-permanent Security Council member for 2025-2026 (Pakistan, Somalia and Denmark were elected; Sri Lanka was not). Not taught: the specific 2025-26 election result is time-bound current affairs and appears in none of this chapter's fetched sources; the chapter teaches Council composition and India's terms only.

Real WBP Constable 2021 item: which country was President of the UN Security Council for August 2021 (answer: India). Not taught in that specificity: the chapter teaches India's eight Council terms including 2021-22 (c39, c46), but the August 2021 presidency month is not stated in any fetched source.

Real WBCS 2018 prelims item: the day celebrated every year on 5 December by FAO (answer: World Soil Day). Not taught: this is an observance-days fact belonging to the Important Days book, and FAO itself is one of the bodies whose details could not be verified from this chapter's fetched sources.
